title: The vortex electron vs Bell: local hidden variables to the ceiling
headline: Every local hidden-variable variant saturates |S|=2; nature measures ~2.4–2.7. Two-particle locality is dead.

claims.claim: The friction-vortex response rule (outcome = sign(axis · current), deterministic or stochastic) reproduces single-particle spin statistics
claims.evidence: [vortex-bell](../../orrery/lab/sims/vortex-bell/) `vortex_bell.py` — contextual single-spin behavior works, echoing Bell's own 1964 single-spin model

claims.claim: The same rule reproduces two-particle Bell correlations
claims.evidence: [vortex-bell](../../orrery/lab/sims/vortex-bell/): optimized over all detector settings, \|S\| saturates at exactly 2.000; E(22.5°) = −0.75 vs QM's −0.924; corkscrew and tilt-enumeration variants (`corkscrew_bell.py`, `tilt_enumeration.py`) hit the same ceiling

claims.claim: Nature itself respects the \|S\| ≤ 2 ceiling (so the model could still be right)
A tabletop analog (ping-pong balls with hidden tilt axes) demonstrates the classical ceiling empirically
claims.evidence: [pingpong-bell](../../orrery/lab/sims/pingpong-bell/): protocol + analysis give \|S\| = 1.49 ± 0.17 on sample data — within the classical bound, as any local mechanism must be (protocol: almanac `20-projects/pingpong-bell/`)
